paragraphs.title: A Call for Zion to Rise from Exile

easy.explanation: The command is addressed to Zion.
easy.q: To whom is the command “Awake, awake” addressed?

easy.explanation: Jerusalem is told, “Shake thyself from the dust.”
easy.q: What is Jerusalem told to shake off?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ye shall be redeemed without money.”
easy.q: With what shall Israel be redeemed?

answers: Israel was sold for nothing and will be redeemed without payment
Israel was sold for money and must pay again
medium.explanation: The people were sold “for nought,” and they will be redeemed “without money.”
medium.q: What connection does Isaiah make between Israel being sold and being redeemed?

medium.explanation: The bands represent bondage that Jerusalem is commanded to cast off.
medium.q: What does “loose thyself from the bands of thy neck” mean?

medium.explanation: The Lord says, “Therefore my people shall know my name.”
medium.q: What does the Lord say His people shall know?

answers: Awakening, rising, and being freed from bondage
Fleeing, paying, and returning to Egypt
challenge.explanation: Jerusalem is told to awaken, rise from the dust, and loose the bands from her neck.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes Jerusalem’s deliverance?

answers: They are suffering under oppressive rulers
challenge.explanation: The people’s rulers cause them to cry out in distress.
challenge.q: What does the statement that Israel’s rulers “make them to howl” reveal about the people’s condition?

answers: Israel is taken for nothing and God’s name is blasphemed, so He will reveal who He is
There is no relationship between them
God’s name is hidden because a payment is required
challenge.explanation: Because His people are oppressed and His name is continually blasphemed, God declares that His people will know His name.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the wrong done to Israel and the revelation of God’s name?

paragraphs.title: The Announcement of Redemption and God's Return to Zion

easy.explanation: The messenger publishes peace, good tidings, and salvation.
easy.q: What does the messenger publish upon the mountains?
What message is proclaimed to Zion?

easy.explanation: The watchmen lift up their voice and sing together.
easy.q: Who lift up their voice together?

medium.explanation: The watchmen see the Lord bringing Zion again.
medium.q: What do the watchmen see in Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: The messenger announces peace, goodness, and salvation.
medium.q: What is a person who brings “good tidings”?

answers: The Lord has comforted His people and redeemed Jerusalem
The people have abandoned the city
medium.explanation: The verse gives the reason: “The Lord hath comforted his people, he hath redeemed Jerusalem.”
medium.q: Why are the waste places of Jerusalem told to break forth into joy?

answers: A messenger announces it, the watchmen witness it, and all nations see it
It remains known only among kings
It is proclaimed only in Egypt
challenge.explanation: The message begins with the messenger and watchmen, then reaches all the ends of the earth.
challenge.q: How does the message of redemption expand from the mountains to the whole earth?

answers: The watchmen directly witness the Lord’s return to Zion
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes clear and direct observation.
challenge.q: What does “they shall see eye to eye” emphasize?

answers: God reveals His power, and the nations witness His salvation
God hides His power, so there is no salvation
challenge.explanation: The Lord reveals His holy power before the nations, and all the earth sees His salvation.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the Lord making bare His holy arm and the nations seeing salvation?

paragraphs.title: A Pure and Peaceful Departure from Exile

answers: From there and from the midst of her
easy.explanation: They are told to go out from there and from the midst of her.
easy.q: From where are the exiles commanded to depart?

easy.explanation: They are called “they that bear the vessels of the Lord.”
easy.q: What do the departing people carry?

easy.explanation: The Lord promises, “I will go before you.”
easy.q: Who goes before the departing people?

answers: They bear the vessels of the Lord
medium.explanation: They must be clean because they bear the Lord’s vessels.
medium.q: Why must the departing people be clean?

answers: Purify themselves and separate from uncleanness
medium.explanation: They are told to touch no unclean thing and to be clean.
medium.q: What does “be ye clean” command the people to do?

medium.explanation: The passage says they will not go out with haste or by flight.
medium.q: How is the departure of the exiles described?

answers: He goes before them and serves as their rear guard
He sends them away without guidance
challenge.explanation: The Lord goes before them, and the God of Israel is their reward, or rear guard.
challenge.q: What twofold role does God have during the people’s departure?

answers: The departure is secure and orderly rather than frantic
challenge.explanation: Because God leads and protects them, they do not need to flee in panic.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the contrast between haste and the Lord’s guidance?

answers: Departure, cleansing, bearing the Lord’s vessels, and divine guidance
challenge.explanation: The people depart, avoid uncleanness, carry the Lord’s vessels, and travel under His guidance.
challenge.q: Which order of ideas appears in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Servant of God Exalted after Humiliation

answers: He will deal prudently and be greatly exalted
easy.explanation: The servant will be exalted, extolled, and very high.
easy.q: What will happen to the Lord’s servant?

answers: His visage was marred and his form was less than that of men
He appeared as a wealthy king
He appeared as a messenger of peace
easy.explanation: His visage was marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men.
easy.q: How did the servant appear to many people?

easy.explanation: Many nations will be sprinkled, and kings will shut their mouths at him.
easy.q: Who will be astonished by what happens to the servant?

answers: Humiliation in the past and exaltation in the future
Peace in the past and war in the future
Wealth in the past and poverty in the future
medium.explanation: Although the servant was greatly disfigured, he will ultimately be exalted.
medium.q: What is the main contrast in the description of the servant?
What does “astonied” mean in the statement that many were astonied at him?

answers: They will be amazed by what they see and consider
medium.explanation: They will see and consider something that had not previously been told or heard.
medium.q: Why will the kings shut their mouths at the servant?

answers: The servant’s future success changes the nations’ and kings’ view of him
challenge.explanation: The servant’s exaltation causes rulers and nations to respond with astonishment and respect.
challenge.q: What makes the transition from disgrace to exaltation possible?

answers: The event will be visible and significant to both peoples and rulers
Only the servant will see it
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that both nations and kings will encounter this unexpected revelation.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that nations will see and kings will consider?

answers: It emphasizes the novelty and wonder of what they witness
It shows that the kings already knew it
It removes the importance of the event
challenge.explanation: The wording stresses that the servant’s exaltation is unprecedented and surprising.
challenge.q: How does the repeated idea of what had not been told or heard explain the kings’ reaction?
